format.note: The activation finding requires adjustment order or rounding to be unclear, whereas given/when cover any new or changed payable calculation. A calculation with clear order and rounding but floating-point amounts or excessive credit consumption still needs this rule. Observability labels and concrete examples are otherwise appropriate.

generality.note: The monetary calculation shape and examples apply across domains; no application-specific recipe is imposed.

decisionUseful.note: The implementation guidance is concrete, but it never explicitly requires documenting the default adjustment order. Documentation is required only when taking the exception.

missing: An explicit requirement to document the adjustment order even when using the default order.
extraObligations: The evidence statement 'the route only parses input, calls the function and serialises the result' restricts all route responsibilities. The spec only requires keeping the calculation out of the route; it does not prohibit authorization, orchestration, or other non-calculation work there.

requiredFixes: Align activation with given/when: activate for new or changed payable calculations without requiring unclear order or rounding, or use a finding that includes every covered violation.
Explicitly require documenting the adjustment order in coder-facing guidance, including the default order.
Replace the route-only responsibility restriction with a check that the route delegates monetary calculation to the pure domain function.
audit.summary: The convention is general, concrete, and free of prohibited application-specific leakage. It needs aligned activation, an explicit default-order documentation requirement, and a narrower route evidence statement before passing.
